title: Leaving Kirby; Kirby as a bandleader
summary: The band was a clique; Kirby lacked experience with keys, let sidemen dictate the drum backing, and played string bass at the Onyx.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Now, you left Kirby, and according to Chilton (of course, I'd like to know from you, because you were the one doing it), you started free-lancing as a drummer after you were with Kirby. Why did you decide to... How was it that you left John Kirby?

Well, that was kind of what you call a clique band. If the boss liked you, you're all right; if he didn't like you, you wouldn't be there very long. But I proved myself inside of two years, because I found out what different ones would like me to play behind them to make them feel happy. Some of them would like the cymbals, some would like wire-brushes, some of them would like the snare drums, some of them liked the woodblock -- different things, you know. Anything to make them feel happy, make them feel good, and make them play good.
Of course, John Kirby, he wasn't too much...wasn't no... He wasn't a bandleader at all.

Well, he just didn't have that much experience. He didn't know different keys. The other boys in the band had to come out on the different keys, especially the piano player. Of course, he was with Fletcher Henderson a long time, you know. He was the bass player for Fletcher Henderson. He played tuba, and the string bass on the side. But mostly he specialized in tuba. But when he went down to the Onyx Club, he was using string bass.
Did he use the tuba, by the way, at the Onyx Club?
No, he didn't use no tuba there. All string bass.
